subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Hydatidiform Mole: Complete, Partial and Snowstorm Appearance

steps.tx: Abnormal fertilisation producing swollen chorionic villi and no normal fetus forms a **hydatidiform mole**. It is the commonest gestational trophoblastic disease. Evacuation and hormone surveillance cure the great majority without chemotherapy. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Hydatidiform mole produces swollen villi without a normal fetus and usually cures with evacuation.

steps.tx: A mole with only paternal chromosomes, usually forty six XX from an empty egg, is a **complete mole**. No fetus exists and villi swell diffusely like grapes. Malignant sequelae follow in about fifteen to twenty percent. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: A complete mole carries only paternal chromosomes and no fetus, with diffuse grape like villi.

steps.tx: A mole with three chromosome sets and an abnormal fetus present is a **partial mole**. Triploidy from two sperm fertilising one egg produces focal villous swelling. Malignant change is rare, under five percent. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: A partial mole is triploid with a fetus present and rarely becomes malignant.

steps.tx: The classic ultrasound picture of innumerable cystic spaces filling the uterus is the **snowstorm appearance**. Modern early scanning more often shows a complex intrauterine mass before this develops. Very high hCG and a uterus large for dates support the diagnosis. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: The snowstorm appearance fills the uterus with cystic spaces on ultrasound in molar pregnancy.

steps.tx: Excessive vomiting, early pre-eclampsia before twenty weeks and thyrotoxicosis features point to mole through **hCG excess effects**. The hormone level often exceeds one hundred thousand units. These systemic features resolve after evacuation. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: hCG excess in mole causes severe vomiting, early pre-eclampsia and thyrotoxic features.

steps.tx: Histology distinguishes mole types by villous change and trophoblast proliferation, aided by **p57 staining**. Complete moles lose this maternally expressed stain, partial moles retain it. Accurate typing guides surveillance length. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: p57 staining separates complete moles, which lose it, from partial moles retaining it.

steps.tx: Bleeding in early pregnancy with passage of grape like vesicles is nearly diagnostic, called **vesicle passage**. Most moles today are diagnosed by scan before this classic sign appears. Any vesicles passed are sent for histology. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Passage of grape like vesicles nearly diagnoses mole, though scans now detect most earlier.

steps.tx: Suction evacuation under ultrasound guidance is the treatment of choice, performed as **suction evacuation**. Oxytocics are avoided before evacuation lest trophoblast embolise, then used after. Tissue always goes for histological confirmation. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Suction evacuation treats mole, with oxytocics avoided until evacuation is underway.

steps.tx: Registration with a specialist centre and serial hormone follow up are mandatory after evacuation, termed **central registration**. This safety net catches the minority progressing to neoplasia while hormone remains measurable. Contraception during follow up prevents diagnostic confusion. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Central registration with serial hormone follow up catches molar progression to neoplasia.
